title: Base change of augmented simplicial differential complexes
statement:
Let $R\to R'\to T$ be homomorphisms of commutative rings and let $P_\bullet\xrightarrow{\epsilon}T$ be an augmented simplicial $R$-algebra. Here the simplicial structure consists of face and degeneracy algebra maps satisfying the simplicial identities and commuting with $\epsilon$. Put $Q_n=P_n\otimes_R R'$ with the induced simplicial structure and augmentation $p\otimes a'\mapsto\epsilon(p)a'$ [def-weil-module-base-change]. Use universal differentials [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] and the alternating cochain convention $s(M)^{-n}=M_n$ of [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence]. There is a natural chain isomorphism
$$s(\Omega^1_{P_\bullet/R}\otimes_{P_\bullet}T)\xrightarrow{\sim}s(\Omega^1_{Q_\bullet/R'}\otimes_{Q_\bullet}T),$$
whose degree $-n$ map sends $\mathrm dp\otimes t$ to $\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes t$ and whose inverse sends $\mathrm d(p\otimes a')\otimes t$ to $\mathrm dp\otimes a't$. These maps commute with every face and degeneracy, and are natural for augmentation-preserving maps of simplicial $R$-algebras. They induce an isomorphism of the displayed objects in $D(T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Neither flatness nor a polynomial-resolution hypothesis is required.

source.place: Tag 08QZ (lemma-localize-at-bottom), displayed differential comparison; algebra.tex, Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change), with its universal-derivation formula.

proof.text: Fix $n$, write $P=P_n$, $Q=P\otimes_RR\prime$ and $M=\Omega_{P/R}$. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] to $R\to R\prime$ and $R\to P$. Interchange the two tensor factors by $a\prime\otimes p\mapsto p\otimes a\prime$ (its inverse interchanges them back; both preserve products and the balancing relation). The cited theorem gives a $Q$-linear isomorphism $E:M\otimes_RR\prime\to\Omega_{Q/R\prime}$ with $E(\mathrm dp\otimes a\prime)=a\prime\mathrm d(p\otimes1)$. Here $(p\otimes b\prime)(\omega\otimes a\prime)=p\omega\otimes b\prime a\prime$. Its hypotheses are just the ring maps in the statement.

Using the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], define $c:(M\otimes_RR\prime)\otimes_QT\to M\otimes_PT$ by $(\omega\otimes a\prime)\otimes t\mapsto\omega\otimes a\prime t$, and $j$ in the other direction by $\omega\otimes t\mapsto(\omega\otimes1)\otimes t$. For $q=p\otimes b\prime$, the two $Q$-balanced representatives for $c$ give $p\omega\otimes b\prime a\prime t=\omega\otimes\epsilon(p)b\prime a\prime t$; additivity extends this to all $q$. The inner $R$-balance follows from the common map $R\to T$. For $j$, $p\omega\otimes1=(p\otimes1)(\omega\otimes1)$ verifies $P$-balance. Both maps are additive and $T$-linear. The composites are identities: $cj(\omega\otimes t)=\omega\otimes t$ and $jc((\omega\otimes a\prime)\otimes t)=(\omega\otimes1)\otimes a\prime t=(\omega\otimes a\prime)\otimes t$. Thus $F_n=(E\otimes_Q1)j$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $c(E^{-1}\otimes_Q1)$; tensoring the inverse identities for $E$ proves the latter claim directly.

source.place: Tag 08QZ (lemma-localize-at-bottom), final displayed tensor identification; explicit balancing argument.

proof.text: The formula for $E$ gives $F_n(\mathrm dp\otimes t)=\mathrm d(p\otimes1)\otimes t$. By the derivation relations [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], $\mathrm d(p\otimes a\prime)=a\prime\mathrm d(p\otimes1)$, because $\mathrm d(1\otimes a\prime)=0$. Therefore $F_n^{-1}(\mathrm d(p\otimes a\prime)\otimes t)=\mathrm dp\otimes a\prime t$. These tensors span: differentials are generated by the symbols $\mathrm dq$, and every $q$ is a finite sum of pure tensors. In particular the formulas specify the maps on the whole modules.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change), derivation formula and proof; universal differential relations.

proof.text: For any augmentation-preserving $R$-algebra map $f:P\to\widetilde P$, the universal property [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials] gives the differential map $\mathrm dp\mapsto\mathrm d(f(p))$: compose the universal derivation of $\widetilde P$ with $f$, which is an $R$-derivation. Augmentation preservation makes its tensor with $T$ well-defined. The two composites with $F$ send each $\mathrm dp\otimes t$ to $\mathrm d(f(p)\otimes1)\otimes t$; by the spanning just proved they agree. Apply this calculation to each face and each degeneracy, and to every component of a morphism of augmented simplicial algebras. This proves the required simplicial compatibility and naturality, including that of the inverses by composing the equality with $F^{-1}$ on both sides.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change), canonical map; preceding functorial-omega construction, with generator calculation written explicitly.

proof.text: In the alternating convention [lem-trf-cotangent-resolution-coherence], put $F^{-n}=F_n$, $G^{-n}=F_n^{-1}$ and use the unique maps between zero modules in positive degrees. The face compatibilities give $F_{n-1}\sum_i(-1)^id_i=\sum_i(-1)^id_iF_n$, and the same for $G$, so these are chain maps. At degree zero both outgoing differentials are zero. The simplicial identity $d_id_j=d_{j-1}d_i$ for $i<j$ cancels paired terms in the square of the alternating differential; no augmentation term is included. The termwise inverse identities give $GF=1$ and $FG=1$ as chain maps. Applying the localization functor defining $D(T)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category] preserves these equations and produces inverse derived morphisms. All constructions used ordinary tensor products and universal derivations; none used flatness, polynomial terms or a resolution.
